::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Febry 10th [1854]  
**From:** [Dogmersfield](organizations/other_121.qmd)  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Caroline Fairclough/2
:::

My dear [Miss Butler](people/person_237.qmd)
Thank you for your message.  I do not think Rudolf requires to return to you for he stands so much alone that he only needs to be taken out.[^1]

Thanks too for the derivations, I shall trouble you with plenty more, I have no doubt, when I am at home with my list, and see my way out of the Latin derived names.[^2]  I am to go home this afternoon after a very happy visit here.  [Elizabeth Barnett](people/person_113.qmd) is writing on the opposite side of the table, I wish I was going to take her back with me.  My [mother](people/person_1606.qmd) is reading your <u>[philosophe](other_books/otherbook_154.qmd)</u> with great delight

yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: CMY had asked Butler to delete a passage from her series of articles *Aunt Louisa's Travels*.
[^2]: CMY had asked Butler's help with Scandinavian names for the series of articles in *[MP](organizations/other_52.qmd)* called 'Name-Fancying' which later became *A History of Christian Names*.
